title: The Quiet Pier
body: Crowe finds you where the cranes sleep. 'Pier 9 after midnight is a church with no God,' he says. 'Don't look. If you look, the Calderas will look back. If you don't, the fire will still happen. I just won't have to watch you in it.'

choices.text: Look anyway.

outcomes.title: A church of crates
outcomes.body: You see sealed boxes with a Caldera wax the color of old blood. A kid on a bike takes a photograph and is gone. Crowe swears without poetry.
outcomes.log: Looked at Pier 9. The Quiet Pier looked back.

choices.text: Heed Crowe. Stay inland.

outcomes.title: Faith in a wet coat
outcomes.body: You don't look. Months later you will smell smoke and know the sermon anyway.
outcomes.log: Heeded Crowe about Pier 9.

choices.text: Slip Vale a dock number. No name.

outcomes.title: A number without a priest
outcomes.body: Vale does not thank you. A week later Pier 9 has extra lamps. Crowe stops calling for a season.
outcomes.log: Tipped Vale about Pier 9 without naming Crowe.

title: The Quiet Pier: Crate
body: A crate from Pier 9 appears behind your building like a stray dog. No note. The wax is Caldera red. Opening it is a marriage. Leaving it is a different kind of vow.

choices.text: Open it. Own the night.

outcomes.title: Red wax, gold problem
outcomes.body: Ledgers. A key. A photograph of Cass Caldera laughing in Glassridge. You are in their weather now.
outcomes.log: Opened the Quiet Pier crate.

choices.text: Send it back with a clean lie.

outcomes.title: Returned to the church
outcomes.body: The crate leaves. A week later a Caldera driver nods at you in traffic like you share a joke. You do not.
outcomes.log: Returned the Quiet Pier crate.

title: Docks Fire
body: Pier 9 burns the color of old gold. Sirens arrive late on purpose. Crowe is there with a wet rag over his mouth. Cass Caldera watches from a black car that does not get dirty. Vale is already counting witnesses. The Quiet Pier has become a headline.

choices.text: Pull people out. Let the ledgers burn.

outcomes.title: A fire that remembers kindness
outcomes.body: You come out coughing with a stranger's kid and no evidence. Crowe squeezes your shoulder hard enough to bruise. Vale sees it. So does Cass.
outcomes.log: Pulled people from the Docks Fire. Let the paper burn.

choices.text: Save the books. Let the smoke take the rest.

outcomes.title: Ash and advantage
outcomes.body: You get a satchel out. It will make you money and a list of people who will not forgive the smell on it.
outcomes.log: Saved ledgers from the Docks Fire.

choices.text: Watch Cass instead of the flames.

outcomes.title: Heir to heir
outcomes.body: Cass mouths one word through glass: LATER. You will hold them to it.
outcomes.log: Watched Cass Caldera during the Docks Fire.

title: Crow Ledger
body: Crowe's apartment is all ashtrays and ferry schedules. He sets a bound book on the table — black, gold thread, no title. 'Every surname that lasts in Ravenport is in here twice: once as they wanted, once as they were. I'll let you write one line. Don't waste it on poetry.'

choices.text: Write the true line.

outcomes.title: Ink that doesn't flinch
outcomes.body: You write what you did at Pier 7 and who you didn't tell. Crowe closes the book like a coffin that still has manners.
outcomes.log: Wrote a true line in the Crow Ledger.

choices.text: Write a kinder fiction.

outcomes.title: A prettier corpse
outcomes.body: The line is elegant and false. Crowe leaves it. The book knows. Books always know.
outcomes.log: Wrote a kinder fiction in the Crow Ledger.

title: Crow Ledger: A Second Hand
body: Years later the book is in someone else's apartment. A page with your line is dog-eared. Cass Caldera has been reading. Or Vale. Or your sibling. Crowe is in the hospital with a cough that sounds like a dock crane.

choices.text: Take the book back.

outcomes.title: Returned to the crow
outcomes.body: You get it. You also get seen. Crowe, when you show him, cries without permission.
outcomes.log: Reclaimed the Crow Ledger.

choices.text: Let them keep the page. Change the story elsewhere.

outcomes.title: A story with copies
outcomes.body: You leave it. Control is a rumor. You spend the year making better rumors.
outcomes.log: Left the Crow Ledger in other hands.

title: Crow Ledger: Close
body: Crowe asks you to sit. The book — or its absence — sits between you. 'When I go,' he says, 'don't put me in the Hall like furniture. Put me in the rain.' Then he asks whether you still keep names.

choices.text: Keep names. Keep the weather.

outcomes.title: The crow's last lesson
outcomes.body: You promise. He believes you this time, which is either wisdom or fatigue.
outcomes.log: Promised Crowe you would keep names.

choices.text: Burn whatever's left of the ledger.

outcomes.title: Ash for the crow
outcomes.body: Paper becomes weather. Crowe laughs until it becomes a cough. 'Cleaner than most endings.'
outcomes.log: Burned the Crow Ledger.

title: Sibling Split
body: Your sibling sits on the fire escape like the city owes them an apology. 'I can go legal,' they say. 'Or I can go with you. Or I can go to the Marrow Kin, who at least pretend not to be a family.' The rain makes every option sound expensive.

choices.text: Keep them close. Make it a vow.

outcomes.title: A second spine
outcomes.body: They stay. The apartment gets louder. So does your luck.
outcomes.log: Kept a sibling close after the Split.

choices.text: Push them toward daylight books.

outcomes.title: A cleaner surname, nearby
outcomes.body: You buy a semester. They look at you like you are both a jailer and a saint.
outcomes.log: Pushed a sibling toward a legal life.

choices.text: Let them take the Marrow meeting.

outcomes.title: Blood on another crest
outcomes.body: They leave with a borrowed jacket. Nessa Marrow sends a courteous note. Courteous is how knives arrive in Harbor Lights.
outcomes.log: Allowed a sibling to meet the Marrow Kin.

title: Sibling Split: The Door
body: Years later they are at your door with a bag and a face that has learned new weather. They want a night's sleep or a job or forgiveness. Possibly all three.

choices.text: Let them in. No speech.

outcomes.title: The door remembers
outcomes.body: You make coffee. The bag stays by the radiator. A dynasty is also a couch.
outcomes.log: Let a sibling back in after the Split.

choices.text: Name terms first.

outcomes.title: Love with a contract
outcomes.body: They agree. They also memorize the cold in your voice.
outcomes.log: Set terms before letting a sibling in.

title: Sibling Split: Table
body: A family table. Someone younger is watching how you pass the bread. Your sibling raises a glass that might be a truce.

choices.text: Toast the split as a scar, not a verdict.

outcomes.title: Scar accepted
outcomes.body: The younger ones laugh. That is the whole point of a table.
outcomes.log: Toasted the Sibling Split as a scar.

choices.text: Remind them who sits at the head.

outcomes.title: A narrower table
outcomes.body: The bread still moves. The warmth does not.
outcomes.log: Used the family table to remind them of the chair.

title: Glass Marriage
body: House Vex sends an invitation printed like a threat: dinner in Midtown glass, rain on the outside, lawyers on the inside. Lior Vex wants a marriage that is also a merger. Cass Caldera will be there, which means the room has two knives and one cake.

choices.text: Go. Wear the rain like jewelry.

outcomes.title: Glass, gold, witnesses
outcomes.body: You are charming because you are afraid in a pretty room. A Vex cousin laughs at your jokes and means some of it.
outcomes.log: Attended the Glass Marriage dinner.

choices.text: Decline. Marry the city instead.

outcomes.title: No merger
outcomes.body: Vex marks you as uninterested in thrones. Cass sends a different kind of smile the next week.
outcomes.log: Declined the Glass Marriage.

title: Glass Marriage: Vows
body: Midtown chapel, rain doing stained glass work. The Vex cousin waits. Cass sits in the back like a rumor with a pulse. Vale is not invited and is somehow still in the parking lot.

choices.text: Make the vows. Merge the weather.

outcomes.title: A marriage that files papers
outcomes.body: You say yes in a room that understands contracts. Love may arrive later, like a late ferry.
outcomes.log: Married through the Glass Marriage.

choices.text: Walk before the ring.

outcomes.title: A scandal with good posture
outcomes.body: You leave. Cass stands as you pass. Vale's car, for once, does not follow.
outcomes.log: Walked out of the Glass Marriage.

title: Red Audit
body: An auditor with immaculate shoes sits in your front like they were born there. 'Irregularities,' they say, as if the word were a hymn. Crowe taught you that clean books create their own trail. Tonight the trail has a clipboard.

choices.text: Open the real books.

outcomes.title: Honesty as a weapon
outcomes.body: You show enough truth to make the lie look expensive. The auditor blinks. Vale will hear a softer version.
outcomes.log: Opened the books for the Red Audit.

choices.text: Stage a prettier ledger.

outcomes.title: Theater with numbers
outcomes.body: It works until it doesn't. The clipboard leaves heavier.
outcomes.log: Staged books for the Red Audit.

title: Red Audit: Verdict
body: Two years of envelopes. The verdict arrives on a Tuesday that smells like rain and photocopiers. Vale is quoted in a paper that does not print your photo. Yet.

choices.text: Pay. Stay a person with a name.

outcomes.title: A fine that buys weather
outcomes.body: You pay. The city files you under expensive and alive.
outcomes.log: Paid the Red Audit. Kept the name above water.

choices.text: Fight it in Vale's weather.

outcomes.title: Crown Prosecutor notices
outcomes.body: You win a delay and a enemy with better stationery. Vale's file thickens like a novel.
outcomes.log: Fought the Red Audit. Vale noticed.

title: Crown Prosecutor
body: Rhea Vale is no longer just a coat in a diner. The office plaque says Crown Prosecutor in a font that wants you tired. She offers coffee again. This time the mug is heavier.

choices.text: Ask what a person costs these days.

outcomes.title: A price list
outcomes.body: Vale names years, not dollars. She is almost kind. Kindness from her is a strategy.
outcomes.log: Heard Vale's price as Crown Prosecutor.

choices.text: Bring a lawyer who hates coffee.

outcomes.title: Professionals in the rain
outcomes.body: Your counsel talks. Vale listens. You feel like furniture in your own life, which is sometimes safer.
outcomes.log: Met Vale with counsel.

title: Crown Prosecutor: Court
body: The eagle on the wall has seen worse. Vale's voice is even. Your name sounds like a city ordinance. The jury looks like people who take ferries.

choices.text: Stand on the story you can live with.

outcomes.title: A city that blinked
outcomes.body: Not guilty enough. Vale nods once, professional. You walk into rain that feels rented.
outcomes.log: Stood in Vale's court and walked.

outcomes.title: Years, counted
outcomes.body: The gavel is quieter than movies. Vale does not look triumphant. That is the insult.
outcomes.log: Took years in Vale's court.

choices.text: Take the years you can spell.

outcomes.title: A known corridor
outcomes.body: You buy certainty. The Hall of Legacy will have to wait in a visiting room.
outcomes.log: Pleaded in Vale's court.

title: The Empty Chair
body: You dream the Hall before you earn it: a long red carpet, gold frames, an empty chair that already has your posture. Waking, you hear the house settle like a jury. Someone younger is asleep down the hall — or isn't.

choices.text: Write the epitaph while you can still lie well.

outcomes.title: A draft for the Hall
outcomes.body: You write three sentences and burn two. The remaining one is almost kind.
outcomes.log: Drafted an epitaph for an empty chair.

choices.text: Refuse the dream. Work the year.

outcomes.title: The chair waits anyway
outcomes.body: You make coffee. The dream files itself under later, which is where all chairs live.
outcomes.log: Ignored the Empty Chair dream.

title: The Empty Chair: Will
body: A lawyer in Westmere wants signatures. The will can leave money, turf, silence, or a fight. The empty chair in the Hall does not care which. The people who will sit in it do.

choices.text: Split it like a family, not a raid.

outcomes.title: A will with manners
outcomes.body: Nobody is thrilled. Everybody can live. That is a kind of empire.
outcomes.log: Wrote a fair will for the empty chair.

choices.text: Name one heir. Let the others become weather.

outcomes.title: A sharp succession
outcomes.body: Clarity is a knife. The Hall will look expensive and lonely.
outcomes.log: Named a single heir in the will.

title: Cass Caldera: Later
body: Cass meant later. A Glassridge terrace, rain on the rail, whiskey the color of the medallion on your city's cheap souvenirs. 'Aurelia thinks you're a weather problem,' Cass says. 'I think you're a door. Doors can be used from both sides.'

choices.text: Make a quiet pact against the old weather.

outcomes.title: Heirs in the rain
outcomes.body: You don't shake hands. You look at the same red window across the water and understand it.
outcomes.log: Made a quiet pact with Cass Caldera.

choices.text: Refuse. Stay a problem, not a door.

outcomes.title: No door
outcomes.body: Cass toasts you anyway. 'Then I'll inherit the view without you.' It does not sound like a joke.
outcomes.log: Refused Cass Caldera's later.
